definition: a small flying insect that bites people and animals and sucks their blood

collocations.example: We slept under a mosquito net to avoid bites.
A mosquito bite on my arm itched all night.

definition: a design, pattern, or idea that is repeated in art, music, or decoration

collocations.example: The wallpaper features a bold geometric motif in blue.
She chose curtains with a delicate floral motif.

definition: the process of shaping a material, especially plastic, in a mould

collocations.example: The parts are made by plastic injection moulding.
The factory specializes in plastic moulding for car parts.

definition: a rounded pile or small raised mass of earth or other material

collocations.example: They dug up the soil and piled it into a mound.
The old castle stands on a grassy mound.

definition: hair that a man grows on his upper lip

collocations.example: The old sailor had a thick, bushy mustache.
He decided to grow a mustache over the winter.

definition: a thick, slippery liquid produced inside the nose and other body parts

collocations.example: A cold makes the nose produce extra nasal mucus.
Thick mucus blocked his nose for several days.

definition: a large cup with a handle, used for hot drinks

collocations.example: She handed me a steaming mug of coffee.
I drank my tea from an old chipped mug.

definition: using several forms of media such as text, sound, pictures, and video together

collocations.example: She gave a multimedia presentation to the whole class.
The website offers rich multimedia content for students.

definition: operating or existing in several different countries

collocations.example: She works for a large multinational company in London.
The firm manages a diverse multinational workforce.

definition: to think about something in a calm, thoughtful way

collocations.example: He likes to muse on life's big questions.
The manager mused aloud about changing the schedule.

definition: to change in form or structure, especially the genes of a living thing

collocations.example: The disease can mutate into a more dangerous form.
Scientists worry that the virus may mutate quickly.

definition: not speaking; silent, especially when a response is expected

collocations.example: The child sat mute in the corner of the room.
He remained mute throughout the long interview.

definition: relating to spiritual or magical mystery beyond ordinary understanding

collocations.example: The stone was said to hold a mystic power.
They performed a strange mystic ritual at dawn.

definition: lacking experience or judgement, and too ready to believe things

collocations.example: It was a naive view of how business really works.
The young candidate seemed politically naive and unprepared.

definition: the legal status of belonging to a particular country

collocations.example: Their children were granted dual nationality at birth.
Workers of foreign nationality need a valid permit.

definition: failing to give proper care or attention, so that harm results

collocations.example: The company was negligent in its safety checks.
The driver was grossly negligent and caused the crash.

definition: the son of your brother or sister

collocations.example: She often babysits her young nephew on weekends.
He left the old house to his beloved nephew.

definition: a specialized and profitable part of a market

collocations.example: The company targets a small but profitable niche market.
They found a niche selling handmade leather bags.

definition: an informal, often friendly name used instead of a real name

collocations.example: His childhood nickname was Tiger, and it stuck.
The new player was given a funny nickname.

definition: the daughter of your brother or sister

collocations.example: He looked affectionately at his young niece.
She traveled far to meet her newborn niece.

definition: a colorless gas that forms most of the air and is a chemical element

collocations.example: The sample was quickly frozen in liquid nitrogen.
Farmers spread nitrogen fertilizer to boost crop growth.

definition: very small in amount, much less than the real value

collocations.example: Members pay only a nominal fee each year.
We pay a nominal rent for the small office.

definition: a person who has been formally proposed for a position, honor, or award

collocations.example: The party chose its presidential nominee last night.
Every award nominee received a letter of congratulation.

definition: to tell someone about something officially or formally

collocations.example: Please notify us of any change of address.
Staff must notify their manager immediately after an accident.

definition: at the present time, especially compared with the past

collocations.example: Working from home is quite common nowadays.
Handwritten letters have become rather rare nowadays.

definition: the central part of an atom or of a living cell

collocations.example: The cell nucleus contains the genetic material.
Protons and neutrons sit inside the atomic nucleus.

definition: not wearing any clothes; naked

collocations.example: She refused to pose nude for the magazine.
The art class sketched a nude model.

definition: a person, thing, or situation that causes trouble or annoyance

collocations.example: Loud late-night parties can become a public nuisance.
The broken lift is a real nuisance.

definition: unable to feel anything, physically or emotionally

collocations.example: My fingers went numb in the freezing wind.
She was numb with cold after the long walk.

definition: relating to, or expressed as, numbers

collocations.example: Each item is assigned a numeric value.
Type the code using the numeric keypad.

definition: a woman who lives in a religious community and has made religious vows

collocations.example: She decided to become a nun at twenty.
A Buddhist nun lives quietly at the mountain temple.

definition: to care for and help something or someone grow and develop

collocations.example: Good teachers nurture talent in their young students.
It takes time to nurture a strong relationship.

definition: a substance in food that living things need to grow and stay healthy

collocations.example: Iron is an essential nutrient for the body.
This label shows the nutrient content of the food.

definition: a formal, solemn promise, often to tell the truth or be loyal

collocations.example: New citizens take an oath of loyalty.
The witness gave her evidence under oath.

definition: offensive or shocking, especially in a sexual way

collocations.example: He was fined for using obscene language in public.
The magazine was banned for printing obscene photographs.

definition: the young or children produced by a person, animal, or plant

collocations.example: Healthy animals usually produce stronger offspring.
Well-fed birds tend to raise healthy offspring.

definition: the beginning of something, especially something unpleasant

collocations.example: Doctors watch for the early onset of the disease.
The sudden onset of winter caught farmers unprepared.

definition: best or most favorable; producing the best possible result

collocations.example: The team searched for the optimal solution to the problem.
Athletes train hard to reach optimal performance.

definition: a feeling of hope and confidence that good things will happen

collocations.example: The report expressed cautious optimism about the economy.
Recent sales figures give real grounds for optimism.

definition: to find your position or become familiar with a new situation

collocations.example: She paused to orient herself before choosing a direction.
New employees must orient to the company rules quickly.

definition: a small object used as decoration rather than for a practical purpose

collocations.example: She hung a shiny Christmas ornament on the tree.
A small decorative ornament stood on the shelf.

definition: a child whose parents have both died

collocations.example: The young orphan was adopted by a kind family.
The couple chose to raise an orphan from the village.

definition: completely and without any doubt or delay

collocations.example: Neither candidate managed to win the election outright.
The board rejected the proposal outright.

definition: the beginning or start of something

collocations.example: Explain the rules clearly at the outset of the game.
The project faced problems from the very outset.

definition: shaped like an egg or a flattened circle

collocations.example: The old mirror had a smooth oval shape.
She has an oval face and dark eyes.

definition: to use your authority to reject or cancel a decision

collocations.example: Congress voted to override the president's veto.
The manager can override the committee's decision.

definition: done or shown openly, not hidden or secret

collocations.example: There was no overt hostility between the two teams.
The mayor gave overt support to the new plan.

definition: the removal of a leader or government from power, usually by force

collocations.example: The rebels planned the overthrow of the government.
Several officers were accused of plotting an overthrow.

definition: a short, general description of something without the details

collocations.example: The manager gave a brief overview of the plan.
The book opens with a historical overview of the war.

definition: a formal agreement between two or more people or groups

collocations.example: The two nations signed a trade pact.
They agreed to a non-aggression pact last year.

definition: to move a small boat through water using a paddle

collocations.example: They paddled the canoe across the calm lake.
We paddled across the river before sunset.

definition: a friend

collocations.example: She writes to her pen pal in Japan.
He went fishing with his best pal.

definition: a piece of clothing covering the legs and lower body; trousers

collocations.example: He bought a new pair of pants yesterday.
She wore brown corduroy pants and a white shirt.

definition: an informal, affectionate word for your father

collocations.example: My papa reads me a story every night.
Papa and Mama worked together on the farm.

definition: the usual or expected standard or level

collocations.example: His recent work has been well below par.
Their service is on a par with the best hotels.

definition: a typical model, pattern, or way of thinking about something

collocations.example: The discovery caused a paradigm shift in medicine.
Managers are adopting a new paradigm of teamwork.

definition: a perfect or ideal place that gives great pleasure

collocations.example: The small island is a quiet tropical paradise.
This busy street is a real shopper's paradise.

definition: to make a person, place, or system unable to move or work

collocations.example: Heavy snow can paralyze the whole city overnight.
A long strike could paralyze the country's economy.

definition: a living thing that lives on or inside another and feeds off it

collocations.example: The dog was treated for an intestinal parasite.
Mosquitoes can carry a dangerous blood parasite.

definition: an object or objects wrapped in paper to be sent or carried

collocations.example: She carefully wrapped the parcel in brown paper.
I need to post a parcel at lunchtime.

definition: strongly supporting one particular party, group, or side

collocations.example: The decision had nothing to do with partisan politics.
The partisan crowd cheered only their own team.

definition: an official document that proves identity and allows foreign travel

collocations.example: You need a valid passport to board the plane.
We waited in a long line at passport control.

definition: an Italian food made from flour and water, such as spaghetti

collocations.example: She ordered a large bowl of pasta.
He learned to cook pasta from his grandmother.

definition: a soft, thick, moist mixture, often used in cooking

collocations.example: Add a spoonful of tomato paste to the sauce.
Mix the flour and water into a smooth paste.

definition: (of a color) pale and soft rather than bright

collocations.example: The nursery was painted in soft pastel colors.
She wore a pretty dress in pale pastel blue.

definition: relating to the countryside and a simple, peaceful rural life

collocations.example: The painting shows a peaceful pastoral scene.
He wrote many poems about simple pastoral life.

definition: a mixture of flour, fat, and water, baked to make pies and tarts

collocations.example: The pie was topped with golden puff pastry.
She made a tart with light, flaky pastry.

definition: grassy land where cattle, sheep, or other animals can feed

collocations.example: The cows grazed in the lush green pasture.
Sheep wandered across the open pasture all day.

definition: so poor or weak that it deserves pity or scorn

collocations.example: She made a pathetic attempt to hide her tears.
He gave some pathetic excuse for being late.

definition: a man who is the head of a family or organization

collocations.example: The old man was the respected family patriarch.
The aging patriarch handed the business to his son.

definition: a small, round, green seed eaten as a vegetable

collocations.example: She made a thick pea soup for lunch.
The hailstones were about the size of a pea.

definition: a round fruit with soft yellow-pink skin and sweet, juicy flesh

collocations.example: He picked the ripest peach from the basket.
The peach tree in the garden was covered in blossom.

definition: a lever you press with your foot to control a machine or vehicle

collocations.example: She pressed her foot hard on the brake pedal.
He pushed the gas pedal to speed up.

definition: a person who is walking, especially in a town or on a road

collocations.example: She was knocked down on a pedestrian crossing.
We walked slowly over the narrow pedestrian bridge.

definition: waiting to be decided or settled

collocations.example: Nine cases against the company are still pending.
The merger is on hold while final approval is still pending.

definition: a piece of land almost completely surrounded by water

collocations.example: Vast deserts cover much of the Arabian Peninsula.
A narrow peninsula stretches far into the blue sea.

definition: to sit or rest on something high or narrow

collocations.example: A small bird perched on the garden fence.
The cat liked to perch atop the tall bookshelf.

definition: a pleasant-smelling liquid that people put on their skin

collocations.example: She likes to wear perfume on special days.
He gave her an expensive bottle of perfume.

definition: serious and immediate danger

collocations.example: The sailors were in great peril during the storm.
Ignore the safety rules at your peril.

definition: to treat someone cruelly or unfairly, especially for their beliefs

collocations.example: The regime began to persecute religious minorities.
People were persecuted for their political beliefs.

definition: the act of making someone agree to do or believe something

collocations.example: He had to use all his powers of persuasion.
After a little gentle persuasion, she finally agreed.

definition: an insect or small animal that damages crops, food, or property

collocations.example: They hired a pest control company for the restaurant.
This spray kills the insect pest without harming plants.

definition: a chemical used to kill insects and other pests that harm crops

collocations.example: Farmers spray pesticide to protect their growing crops.
Tests found some pesticide residue on the fruit.

definition: oil found underground that is refined into fuel and other products

collocations.example: Fuel and plastics are common petroleum products.
Thousands of workers depend on the petroleum industry.

definition: small and unimportant; concerned with trivial matters

collocations.example: She felt trapped by all their petty rules.
They had a petty argument over the bill.

definition: relating to the production and sale of medicines and drugs

collocations.example: She works for a large pharmaceutical company.
New rules will affect the whole pharmaceutical industry.

definition: a scientist who studies physics

collocations.example: Her father was a famous nuclear physicist.
The theoretical physicist explained the new model clearly.

definition: a small truck with an open back for carrying loads

collocations.example: He loaded the heavy boxes into his pickup truck.
A red pickup was parked outside the old barn.

definition: a meal that you pack and eat outdoors for pleasure

collocations.example: We plan to go on a picnic tomorrow.
She packed the sandwiches into the picnic basket.

definition: a long structure built out into water for boats or for walking

collocations.example: We walked to the end of the wooden pier.
Tourists strolled along the pier at sunset.

definition: to make a hole in or through something with a sharp point

collocations.example: The sharp needle can easily pierce the skin.
Use a pin to pierce a small hole.

definition: a gray bird often seen in towns and city squares

collocations.example: The urgent message was sent by carrier pigeon.
A flock of pigeons gathered in the square.

definition: a tall, solid upright post that supports a building

collocations.example: The heavy roof rested on four thick stone pillars.
Tall marble pillars lined the grand entrance.

definition: a unit for measuring liquid, equal to about half a liter

collocations.example: He ordered a pint of beer at the bar.
She drank half a pint of milk.

definition: a long pipe used to carry oil, gas, or water over a distance

collocations.example: A new gas pipeline will cross the border.
Rebels damaged the main oil pipeline overnight.

definition: a person who attacks and robs ships at sea

collocations.example: The children played on the wooden pirate ship.
A band of pirates attacked the merchant vessel.

definition: a small gun that is held and fired with one hand

collocations.example: The officer fired his pistol into the air.
He kept a loaded pistol in the drawer.

definition: a fixed point or pin on which something turns or balances

collocations.example: The lever moves around a central pivot point.
The pedal had sheared off at the pivot pin.

definition: a flat, round bread baked with tomato, cheese, and toppings

collocations.example: Let's order a pizza for dinner tonight.
He grabbed a hot slice of pizza.
